title: UK ‘Most Expensive Place’ to Build Nuclear Power, Review Finds

sentences: The UK has become the "most expensive place in the world" to build a nuclear power station because of overly complex bureaucracy and regulation, according to a government review.
translations: 根据一份政府审查报告，由于过于复杂的官僚体系和监管，英国已成为世界上建造核电站“最昂贵的地方”。

sentences: The nuclear regulatory taskforce was set up by Keir Starmer in February after the government promised to rip up "archaic rules" and slash regulations to "get Britain building".
translations: 核监管工作组由基尔·斯塔默于2月成立，此前政府承诺废除“过时规则”并大幅削减法规，以“让英国建设起来”。

sentences: It issued a stark warning on Monday, warning that Britain needed a "radical reset" of the rules around nuclear power to save "tens of billions" in costs and reverse the industry's decline.
translations: 周一，它发出严厉警告，称英国需要对核电规则进行“彻底重置”，以节省“数百亿”成本并扭转该行业的衰退。

sentences: The review blamed a "fragmented" regulatory system that had led to "conservative and costly decisions not proportionate to the actual risk being managed".
translations: 该审查指责一个“碎片化”的监管体系导致了“保守且代价高昂的决策，与所管理的实际风险不成比例”。

sentences: The taskforce was led by John Fingleton, the former head of the Office of Fair Trading.
He said of the final report: "Our solutions are radical, but necessary.
By simplifying regulation, we can maintain or enhance safety standards while finally delivering nuclear capacity safely, quickly, and affordably."
translations: 该工作组由公平贸易办公室前负责人约翰·芬格尔顿领导。
他在谈到最终报告时表示：“我们的解决方案虽然激进，但却是必要的。
通过简化监管，我们可以在维持或提高安全标准的同时，最终安全、快速且经济地实现核能产能。”

sentences: It published its interim report in August, which led a coalition of 25 civil society groups to warn of the dangers of cutting nuclear safety regulations.
It said the proposals lacked "credibility and rigour".
translations: 它于八月发布了中期报告，这导致由25个民间社会团体组成的联盟警告削减核安全法规的危险。
它表示这些提案缺乏“可信度和严谨性”。

sentences: The latest recommendations include restructuring the nuclear industry's regulatory bodies to create a single commission for nuclear regulation, and changing environmental and planning regimes "to enhance nature and deliver projects quicker".
translations: 最新的建议包括重组核工业监管机构，以创建一个单一的核监管委员会，并改变环境和规划制度，“以改善自然并更快地交付项目”。

sentences: Fingleton said Britain's regulations had "made us the most expensive place in the world to build nuclear", telling BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "Motorways wouldn't be very useful if we all drove at five miles an hour but that's sort of what we're doing in nuclear safety."
translations: 芬格尔顿表示，英国的法规"使我们成为世界上建设核电站最昂贵的地方"，他在接受BBC广播4台《今日》节目采访时说："如果大家都以每小时5英里的速度行驶，高速公路就不会有多大用处，但这正是我们在核安全方面所做的。"

sentences: Ed Miliband, the energy secretary, said the new rules would form a crucial part of delivering the changes needed to drive new nuclear "in a safe, affordable way".
translations: 能源大臣埃德·米利班德表示，新规定将成为实现所需变革的关键部分，以“安全、经济的方式”推动新的核能发展。

sentences: The report was welcomed by Tom Greatrex, the chief executive of the Nuclear Industry Association.
He said the report represented an "unprecedented opportunity to make nuclear regulation more coherent, transparent and efficient" that could make projects "faster and less expensive to deliver".
translations: 该报告受到了核工业协会首席执行官汤姆·格雷特雷克斯的欢迎。
他表示，该报告代表了“一个前所未有的机会，使核监管更加连贯、透明和高效”，这可能使项目“交付更快、成本更低”。

sentences: "Too often, costly and bureaucratic processes have stood in the way of our energy security, the fight against the climate crisis, and protecting the natural environment, to which nuclear is essential," he added.
translations: 他补充道：“过于频繁地，昂贵且官僚的程序阻碍了我们的能源安全、应对气候危机的斗争以及保护自然环境，而核能对此至关重要。”

sentences: Sam Richards, the chief executive of the pro-nuclear campaign group Britain Remade, said it could mark "a watershed moment for cutting the cost of new nuclear in Britain".
translations: 支持核能的运动组织“英国再造”的首席执行官萨姆·理查兹表示，这可能标志着“降低英国新核电成本的一个分水岭时刻”。

sentences: "The findings of the taskforce lay bare the litany of regulations that make Britain the most expensive place in the world to build nuclear power stations," Richards said.
translations: 理查兹表示：“工作组的调查结果揭示了大量法规，这些法规使英国成为世界上建造核电站最昂贵的地方。”

sentences: At a time when Britain's electricity bills are among the world's highest, our regulatory system forced EDF to spend nearly £280,000 per fish protected.
This is indefensible.
These types of modifications have added years in construction and billions in costs; costs that ultimately get passed on to consumers in higher bills.
translations: 在英国电费位居世界最高之列之际，我们的监管体系迫使法国电力公司为每一条受保护的鱼花费近28万英镑。
这是不可原谅的。
这类修改导致建设工期延长数年，成本增加数十亿英镑；而这些成本最终通过更高的账单转嫁给消费者。

sentences: Fingleton added: "This is a once in a generation opportunity."
The problems are systemic, rooted in unnecessary complexity, and a mindset that favours process over outcome.
translations: 芬格尔顿补充道：“这是一个千载难逢的机会。”
这些问题具有系统性，源于不必要的复杂性，以及一种重过程轻结果的心态。

sentences: Mike Finnerty, the chief executive of the Office for Nuclear Regulation and chief nuclear inspector, said the taskforce's findings had informed the development of new regulation strategy, which would be published for public consultation next month.
translations: 核监管办公室首席执行官兼首席核检查员迈克·芬纳蒂表示，工作组的调查结果已为新监管策略的制定提供了依据，该策略将于下月公布以征求公众意见。

sentences: He said it would set out a "modern, agile and productive regulatory approach" with public trust and strong safety standards at its heart.
translations: 他表示，这将提出一种“现代、灵活且高效的监管方法”，其核心是公众信任和严格的安全标准。
